rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their awakening, like their sleep, displays God’s power over both sleep and resurrection, prompts inquiry, reflection and certainty, and calls for gratitude.
rows.anchor: وكما أنمناهم تلك النومة كذلك بعثناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their estimate of a day or part of one rests on predominant conjecture; this permits ijtihad and probable judgment, which may be mistaken without being a lie.
rows.anchor: جواب مبني على غالب الظن . وفيه دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والقول بالظن الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some correct the others: the duration was long, known only to God, perhaps inferred from evidence or divine inspiration.
rows.anchor: إنكار عليهم من بعضهم ، وأن الله أعلم بمدة لبثهم

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: They entered the cave in the morning and awoke after noon, first supposing it was still the same day; their long nails and hair prompted their estimate.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وكان انتباههم بعد الزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turn to sending someone for food means they stop debating an unknowable duration and attend to a more urgent need.
rows.anchor: لا طريق لكم إلى علمه ، فخذوا في شيء آخر مما يهمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wariq means silver, whether minted or unminted.
rows.anchor: والورق : الفضة ، مضروبة كانت أو غير مضروبة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says ʿArfaja lost his nose at the battle of al-Kulab, tried a silver replacement that smelled, and was ordered to use gold.
rows.anchor: أن عرفجة أصيب أنفه يوم الكلاب فاتخذ أنفا من ورق فأنتن ، فأمره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wariq is read with the ra still or moving; Ibn Kathir has kasra on ra and assimilates qaf into kaf.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بورقكم ) بسكون الراء والواو مفتوحة أو مكسورة . وقرأ ابن كثير ( بورقكم ) ، بكسر الراء وإدغام القاف في الكاف

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads waw with kasra, ra still, and assimilation; al-Zamakhshari rejects it as an impermissible meeting of two still letters.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن محيصن أنه كسر الواو وأسكن الراء وأدغم ، وهذا غير جائز لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The city meant is Tarsus.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المدينة طرسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their carrying travel provisions and money exemplifies the prudent reliance of those who trust God, rather than relying on chance or others’ stores.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن حمل النفقة وما يصلح المسافر هو رأي المتوكلين على الله

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Aisha told someone asking about a pilgrim in ihram fastening his money belt to secure his provisions.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عائشة رضي الله عنها لمن سألها عن محرم يشد عليه هميانه : أوثق عليك نفقتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recounts an ascetic scholar who declined wealthy townspeople’s offers to finance pilgrimage, saying travel requires a money belt and trust in the Merciful.
rows.anchor: ما لهذا السفر إلا شيآن : شد الهميان ، والتوكل على الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among them” means among the city’s people, with “people” elided as in the command to ask the town.
rows.anchor: بينهم } أي أهلها ، فحذف الأهل كما في قوله { واسئل القرية }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azka food may mean most lawful, pleasant, abundant, or inexpensive.
rows.anchor: أزكى طعاما } أحل وأطيب وأكثر وأرخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be tactful” may mean taking care in the purchase to avoid being cheated, or keeping discreet so no one recognizes the envoy.
rows.anchor: وليتلطف } وليتكلف اللطف والنيقة فيما يباشره من أمر المبايعة حتى لا يغبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to let anyone know includes avoiding actions that unintentionally cause people to notice them; the wording calls that causing awareness.
rows.anchor: يعني : ولا يفعلن ما يؤدي من غير قصد منه إلى الشعور بنا ، فسمى ذلك إشعارا منه بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they” refers to the implied people of the city in “among them.”
rows.anchor: الضمير في { إنهم } راجع إلى الأهل المقدر في { بينهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They stone you” means kill you by stoning, the vilest killing and their customary method.
rows.anchor: يرجموكم } يقتلوكم أخبث القتلة وهي الرجم ، وكانت عادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or return you to their religion” means they would violently force you back into it; ʿāda often means to become or begin doing something, not literally return.
rows.anchor: أو يعيدوكم } أو يدخلوكم { في ملتهم } بالإكراه العنيف ويصيروكم إليها . والعود في معنى الصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they entered the persecutors’ religion, they would never prosper.
rows.anchor: ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا } إذ دخلتم في دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with their sleep and awakening, God disclosed them for a purpose: to show that the promised resurrection is true, since their experience parallels death and revival.
rows.anchor: وكما أنمناهم وبعثناهم ، لما في ذلك من الحكمة أطلعنا عليهم ، ليعلم الذين أطلعناهم على حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When they dispute” attaches to God’s disclosure: disputants differed over whether resurrection restores souls alone or bodies with souls; the youths’ case proves bodies return alive and sentient.
rows.anchor: بعضهم يقول : تبعث الأرواح دون الأجساد . وبعضهم يقول : تبعث الأجساد مع الأرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading of the dispute is that people discussed the youths’ story and the sign God showed through them.
rows.anchor: يتذاكر الناس بينهم أمر أصحاب الكهف ، ويتكلمون في قصتهم وما أظهر الله من الآية فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another alternative is that, after the youths died, people debated how to hide their place and block access to the cave.
rows.anchor: يتنازعون بينهم تدبير أمرهم حين توفوا ، كيف يخفون مكانهم ؟ وكيف يسدون الطريق إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building over the cave entrance would keep people from approaching their resting place, as an enclosure protected the Prophet’s grave.
rows.anchor: على باب كهفهم . لئلا يتطرق إليهم الناس ضنا بتربتهم ومحافظة عليها كما حفظت تربة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالحظيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prevailed were the Muslims and their king, who had the stronger claim to the youths and the building.
rows.anchor: من المسلمين وملكهم وكانوا أولى بهم وبالبناء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They built a mosque at the cave entrance so Muslims could pray there and seek blessing from the youths’ location.
rows.anchor: على باب الكهف { مسجدا } يصلي فيه المسلمون ويتبركون بمكانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says Daqyanus forced noble youths to worship idols; they fled, and a dog either spoke of loving God’s beloved and offered to guard them or followed them with its shepherd owner, who shared their faith.
rows.anchor: وممن شدد في ذلك دقيانوس ، فأراد فتية من أشراف قومه على الشرك وتوعدهم بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before their awakening, a righteous believing man ruled the city while its people disputed resurrection; he withdrew in sackcloth and ashes and asked God to disclose the truth.
rows.anchor: ملك مدينتهم رجل صالح مؤمن . وقد اختلف أهل مملكته في البعث معترفين وجاحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired a shepherd to open the cave mouth for a sheepfold; the envoy’s old coin led to suspicion of treasure, and his account brought the king and townspeople to witness the sign of resurrection.
rows.anchor: فألقى الله في نفس رجل من رعيانهم فهدم ماسد به فم الكهف ليتخذه حظيرة لغنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths commended the king to God’s protection, returned to their beds, and died; the king changed their gold coffins to teak after seeing in a dream that they disliked gold, then built a mosque.
rows.anchor: ثم رجعوا إلى مضاجعهم وتوفى الله أنفسهم ، فألقى الملك عليهم ثيابه ، وأمر فجعل لكل واحد تابوت من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their Lord knows best” may be the disputants conceding that they cannot establish the youths’ lineage, circumstances, or duration.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يهتدوا إلى حقيقة ذلك قالوا : ربهم أعلم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is God’s rebuttal of speculators, either the contemporaneous disputants or the People of the Book who disputed the story in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: أو هو من كلام الله عز وجل رد لقول الخائضين في حديثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For a thing” means concerning something one resolves to do; “tomorrow” means any future time, not only the next day.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولن لأجل شيء تعزم عليه { إنى فاعل ذالك } الشيء { غدا } أي فيما يستقبل من الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception belongs with the prohibition, not the assertion of intent; otherwise it would suggest God’s will might interrupt the act, which is irrelevant to the warning.
rows.anchor: يشاء الله } متعلق بالنهي لا بقوله : إني فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse means do not say it unless God permits you to say it.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولن ذلك القول إلا أن يشاء الله أن تقوله ، بأن يأذن لك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse makes the exception a circumstantial qualification: say it while invoking God’s will, as in “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: ولا تقولنه إلا بأن يشاء الله ، أي : إلا بمشيئة الله ، وهو في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse treats “unless God wills” as an emphatic “never,” as in the impossible return to the former religion.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولنه أبدا . ونحوه قوله { وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله } ( الأعراف : 89 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse disciplines the Prophet: after Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Cave Companions and Dhul-Qarnayn, he promised an answer next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation was delayed and Quraysh called him a liar.
rows.anchor: سلوه عن الروح ، وعن أصحاب الكهف ، وذي القرنين . فسألوه فقال : ائتوني غدا أخبركم ولم يستثن ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one forgets the exception, one should invoke God when remembering it.
rows.anchor: إذا فرط منك نسيان لذلك . والمعنى : إذا نسيت كلمة الاستثناء ثم تنبهت عليها فتداركها بالذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a delayed exception even after a year, provided the oath has not been broken.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : ولو بعد سنة ما لم تحنث .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr allows the exception after a day, week, month or year.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : ولو بعد يوم أو أسبوع أو شهر أو سنة .

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus limits the exception to the same sitting.
rows.anchor: وعن طاوس : هو على ثنياه ما دام في مجلسه .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to hold the same-sitting limit.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن نحوه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta allows enough time to milk a plentiful she-camel.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء : يستثنى على مقدار حلب ناقة غزيرة .

rows.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
rows.claim: The majority of jurists say a delayed exception has no legal effect unless joined to the original statement.
rows.anchor: وعند عامة الفقهاء أنه لا أثر له في الأحكام ما لم يكن موصولا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: When al-Mansur challenged Abu Hanifa over disagreeing with Ibn Abbas, Abu Hanifa argued that delayed exceptions to oath-bound allegiance would let people leave and then renounce it; al-Mansur approved.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : هذا يرجع عليك ، إنك تأخذ البيعة بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Remember your Lord” may mean praise and seek forgiveness after forgetting, emphasizing care with the exception.
rows.anchor: واذكر ربك بالتسبيح والاستغفار إذا نسيت كلمة الاستثناء ، تشديدا في البعث على الاهتمام بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are to remember God after neglecting part of His command, or when forgetfulness strikes so He recalls the forgotten; this also covers making up a missed prayer upon remembering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : واذكره إذا اعتراك النسيان ليذكرك المنسي ، وقد حمل على أداء الصلاة المنسية عند ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” points to the Cave Companions’ story; the Prophet asks for greater proofs of his prophethood, and God later gives him more compelling prophetic stories and unseen reports.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى نبإ أصحاب الكهف . ومعناه : لعل الله يؤتيني من البينات والحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, when something is forgotten one should remember God and hope He guides one to a better replacement; forgetting may itself be good, as in the abrogation verse.
rows.anchor: إذا نسيت شيئا فاذكر ربك . وذكر ربك عند نسيانه أن تقول : عسى ربي أن يهديني لشيء آخر بدل هذا المنسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated duration is the time they remained alive asleep in the cave, clarifying the earlier account of years spent under the sleep.
rows.anchor: يريد لبثهم فيه أحياء مضروبا على آذانهم هذه المدة ، وهو بيان لما أجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say: God knows best” means God knows their duration better than those disputing it; the truth is what He revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أنه أعلم من الذين اختلفوا فيهم بمدة لبثهم ، والحق ما أخبرك الله به

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the statement quotes the People of the Book, and “God knows best” answers them.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : أنه حكاية لكلام أهل الكتاب . و { قل الله أعلم } رد عليهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the codex of ʿAbdullah, the wording includes “they say: they remained.”
rows.anchor: وقال في حرف عبد الله : وقالوا لبثوا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Years” is an explanatory apposition to three hundred; a reading has the genitive construction with a plural in place of a singular measure, as in 18:103.
rows.anchor: وسنين : عطف بيان لثلثمائة . وقرىء ( ثلثمائة سنين ) ، بالإضافة ، على وضع الجمع موضع الواحد

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading uses the singular “year” after three hundred.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي ( ثلثمائة سنة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nine” means nine years, supplied by the preceding duration.
rows.anchor: تسعا } تسع سنين ؛ لأن ما قبله يدل عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “nine” with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( تسعا ) بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows what is hidden in the heavens and earth; the expressions of seeing and hearing marvelously signal perception beyond human limits, of the tiniest and largest, hidden and visible.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو وحده العالم به ، وجاء بما دل على التعجب من إدراكه المسموعات والمبصرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they have” refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth; a wali is one who manages their affairs.
rows.anchor: مالهم } الضمير لأهل السموات والأرض { له من ولى } من متول لأمورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one shares God’s judgment or decree.
rows.anchor: ولا يشرك في حكمه } في قضائه { أحدا } منهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase as a prohibition addressed to the listener: “do not associate.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ولا تشرك ، بالتاء والجزم على النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When opponents ask for a different Qur’an or alteration, the Prophet is told to recite what was revealed and disregard their demand; no one can change God’s words, though God alone can do so.
rows.anchor: ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله ، فقيل له { واتل ما أوحى إليك } من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will find no refuge apart from Him” means there is nowhere to flee if one intends to comply with their demand.
rows.anchor: ملتجأ تعدل إليه إن هممت بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelieving chiefs asked the Prophet to dismiss poor Muslims such as Suhayb, ʿAmmar and Khabbab so they could sit with him; the request resembles Noah’s people’s objection.
rows.anchor: نح هؤلاء الموالي الذين كأن ريحهم ريح الضأن ، وهم : صهيب وعمار وخباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Restrain yourself” means keep and steady yourself with the poor believers.
rows.anchor: واصبر نفسك } وأحبسها معهم وثبتها

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s verse illustrates patient endurance.
rows.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب : فصبرت عارفة لذلك حرة … ترسوا إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening means constant prayer at all times; another view identifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: بالغداة والعشى } دائبين على الدعاء في كل وقت . وقيل : المراد صلاة الفجر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “at early morning”; “at dawn” is more idiomatic because ghudwa is usually a proper name, while the article here interprets it as indefinite, an uncommon construction illustrated by poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بالغدوة ) وبالغداة أجود ؛ لأن غدوة علم في أكثر الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” uses ʿadā with ʿan by blending the senses of withdrawing and rising above, conveying a gaze that leaps over them toward others; compare 4:2.
rows.anchor: وإنماعدى بعن ، لتضمين عدا معنى نبا وعلا ، في قولك : نبت عنه عينه وعلت عنه عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings make “your eye” singular or use a causative form; a cited line with “turn away from what you see” witnesses the latter sense.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ولا تعد عينيك ، ولا تعد عينيك ) من أعداه نقلا بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is warned against despising poor believers for shabby dress and looking toward the wealthy and their finery.
rows.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يزدرى بفقراء المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seeking the adornment of worldly life” is a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: تريد زينة الحيواة الدنيا } في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whose heart We made heedless” may mean God left it heedless, found it heedless, or left it unmarked by remembrance and faith; its following desire shows that compulsion is not intended.
rows.anchor: من جعلنا قلبه غافلا عن الذكر بالخذلان . أو وجدناه غافلا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading attaches the verb to the heart, meaning it was counted heedless; “following his desire” also describes the person’s own conduct.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( أغفلنا قلبه ) بإسناد الفعل إلى القلب على معنى : حسبنا قلبه غافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faratan describes one who advances beyond truth and sound judgment, casting them behind him, like a horse that runs ahead.
rows.anchor: فرطا } متقدما للحق والصواب نابذا له وراء ظهره من قولهم ( فرس فرط )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “But He is God, my Lord” contracts “but I”; its hamza drops, its vowel transfers to the nun, and the two nuns assimilate.
rows.anchor: أصله لكن أنا ، فحذفت الهمزة وألقيت حركتها على نون لكن ، فتلاقت النونان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem likewise uses “but I” with the initial alif omitted.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قول القائل : وترمينني بالطرف أي أنت مذنب … وتقلينني لكن إياك لا أقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huwa is a pronoun of the matter; the matter is “God my Lord,” and the sentence predicates ana, with the attached ya referring back to it.
rows.anchor: وهو ضمير الشأن ، والشأن الله ربي ، والجملة خبر أنا ، والراجع منها إليه ياء الضمير

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir retains the alif of ana in connected and paused speech; other readers retain it only when pausing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بإثبات ألف أنا في الوصل والوقف جميعا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr pauses with the form “lakinnah.”
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو أنه وقف بالهاء : لكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings include “but He is God my Lord” with a still nun and no ana, Ubayy’s original “but I,” and Abdullah’s expanded confession.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( لكن هو الله ربي ) ، بسكون النون وطرح أنا . وقرأ أبي بن كعب : ( لكن أنا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast answers “Have you disbelieved?”: the speaker tells his brother that he is an unbeliever, while he himself believes in and worships one God.
rows.anchor: قال لأخيه : أنت كافر بالله ، لكني مؤمن موحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whatever God wills” can be a relative clause, with the omitted predicate “the matter is,” or a conditional with omitted result, “whatever God wills comes to pass.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون { ما } موصولة مرفوعة المحل على أنها خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On entering the garden, one should acknowledge that its existence and every good in it depend on God’s will and grace, and that He can preserve or ruin it.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بأنها وكل خير فيها إنما حصل بمشيئة الله وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no strength except through God” confesses that cultivation and management depend on divine support; bodily ability and property are not independent of Him.
rows.anchor: إقرارا بأن ما قويت به على عمارتها وتدبير أمرها إنما هو بمعونته وتأييده

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿUrwa used to open a breach in his garden wall during the date harvest, invite visitors, and repeat this verse while inside.
rows.anchor: وعن عروة بن الزبير أنه كان يثلم حائطه أيام الرطب ، فيدخل من شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative “aqalla,” ana is an emphatic separator; with nominative, ana is the subject and aqallu its predicate, and the clause is the second object of tarani.
rows.anchor: من قرأ { أقل } بالنصب فقد جعل أنا فصلا ، ومن رفع جعله مبتدأ وأقل خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Children” supports understanding nufar in 18:34 as offspring; the believer expects God may reverse their fortunes, granting him a better garden for faith and ruining the other man’s garden for disbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { وولدا } نصرة لمن فسر النفر والأولاد في قوله { وأعز نفرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasaban is a measured amount decreed by God and a judgment to ruin the garden.
rows.anchor: والحسبان : مصدر كالغفران والبطلان ، بمعنى الحساب ، أي : مقدارا قدره الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains hasaban as a punishment accounting for what the owner’s hands earned.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : عذاب حسبان ، وذلك الحسبان حساب ما كسبت يداك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes hasaban as bolts of lightning, each one a hasbanah.
rows.anchor: وقيل حسبانا مرامي الواحدة حسبانة وهي الصواعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slippery plain is smooth, white ground on which one slips; both saʿid and ghawr are verbal nouns used descriptively.
rows.anchor: صعيدا زلقا } أرضا بيضاء يزلق عليها لملاستها زلقا . و { غورا } كلاهما وصف بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water causes earthly plants to intertwine and grow dense.
rows.anchor: فاختلط به نبات الأرض } فالتف بسببه وتكاثف حتى خالط بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that water permeates the vegetation, mixing with it until it is lush; the wording is sound because each of two mixed things can take the other’s quality.
rows.anchor: نجع في النبات الماء فاختلط به حتى روى ورف رفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashim is vegetation broken and crushed; its singular is hashimah.
rows.anchor: والهشيم : ما تهشم وتحطم ، الواحدة هشيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “the wind scatters it”; Ibn Abbas reads “the winds scatter it,” using the causative form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تذروه الريح ) وعن ابن عباس : تذريه الرياح ، من أذرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly life’s freshness and beauty followed by ruin is like lush green growth that withers and blows away as if it never existed.
rows.anchor: شبه حال الدنيا في نضرتها وبهجتها وما يتعقبها من الهلاك والفناء ، بحال النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has power over all things in bringing them into being and making them perish.
rows.anchor: وكان الله على كل شيء } من الإنشاء والإفناء { مقتدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man after kull is adjectival because kull is indefinite, as in a poetic example where rabb is likewise followed by man.
rows.anchor: {من} موصوفة لأنها وقعت بعد كل نكرة ، وقوعها بعد رب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Abu Haywa read “atā al-Raḥmān,” retaining the form before annexation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبوحيوة ( آت الرحمن ) على أصله قبل الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s enumeration means that He encompasses them in His knowledge and counts them one by one.
rows.anchor: الإحصاء الحصر والضبط يعني : حصرهم بعلمه وأحاط بهم { وعدهم عدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who make angels, Jesus or Ezra God’s children commit two errors: saying the Merciful can beget, and worshipping alleged divine offspring; the passage refutes the first and then the second.
rows.anchor: أنهم أولاد الله ، كانوا بين كفرين ، أحدهما : القول بأن الرحمن يصح أن يكون والدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every alleged heavenly or earthly deity comes to the Merciful as a submissive servant, not claiming the divinity attributed by its worshippers.
rows.anchor: إلا وهو يأتي الرحمن ، أي : يأوي إليه ويلتجيء إلى ربوبيته عبدا منقادا مطيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked seek nearness to their Lord, hope for mercy and fear punishment, as in 17:57.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All are ruled by God, who encompasses every detail of their states without missing anything; each will come alone on the Resurrection Day, with the alleged partners disavowing them.
rows.anchor: وكلهم متقلبون في ملكوته مقهورون بقهره وهو مهيمن عليهم محيط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With praise of your Lord” may be a circumstantial phrase: praise Him for enabling and helping you to pray.
rows.anchor: بحمد ربك } في موضع الحال ، أي : وأنت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih means prayer: dawn before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, night prayer, and prayers at the day’s edges.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتسبيح الصلاة . أو على ظاهر قدم الفعل على الأوقات أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the order of time phrases and action conveys prayer at those times; night worship is especially meritorious for focus, quiet, solitude with God, effort and stronger fulfillment of duty, as 73:6 and 39:9 indicate.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل ، لاجتماع القلب وهدو الرجل والخلو بالرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night includes the late prayer, and the day’s edges include Maghrib and Fajr; their repetition marks special status, like the “middle prayer” in 2:238 for some exegetes.
rows.anchor: وقد تناول التسبيح في آناء الليل صلاة العتمة ، وفي أطراف النهار صلاة المغرب وصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Edges of the day” is plural to avoid ambiguity; the dual in 11:114 gives added clarity, like the poetic example of two backs.
rows.anchor: قلت : الوجه أمن الإلباس ، وفي التثنية زيادة بيان . ونظير مجيء الأمرين في الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading coordinates “the edges of the day” with “the hours of night.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأطراف النهار ) عطفا على آناء الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla addresses the Prophet, expressing hope that remembrance at these times brings what satisfies him and gladdens his heart.
rows.anchor: ولعل للمخاطب ، أي : اذكر الله في هذه الأوقات ، طمعا ورجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading makes the verb passive: that your Lord may satisfy you.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ترضى ) أي يرضيك ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disputant as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه أبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated story may be repetition like other narratives, or the first instance may concern imitators and this one another class of imitators.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كرر كما كررت سائر الأقاصيص . وقيل : الأول في المقلدين ، وهذا في المقلدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge means necessary knowledge, guidance means inference and reflection leading to knowledge, and the illuminating Book means revelation; the disputant relies on conjecture instead.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعلم : العلم الضروري . وبالهدى : الاستدلال والنظر ؛ لأنه يهدي إلى المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning one’s side expresses arrogance and swagger; another view takes it as turning away from remembrance.
rows.anchor: وثنى العطف : عبارة عن الكبر والخيلاء ، كتصغير الخد ولي الجيد . وقيل : عن الإعراض عن الذكر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase with fatḥa on ʿayn, meaning that he blocks himself from showing affection.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : ثاني عطفه ، بفتح العين ، أي : مانع تعطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase is read with either a passive or active initial vowel: to mislead or to go astray.
rows.anchor: ليضل } تعليل للمجادلة . قرىء بضم الياء وفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although misguidance may not be the disputant’s stated goal, its result is treated as his goal; because guidance was available but rejected, he is described as leaving it for error.
rows.anchor: لما أدى جداله إلى الضلال ، جعل كأنه غرضه ، ولما كان الهدى معرضا له فتركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His disgrace was the humiliation and death he suffered at Badr; his own past actions caused it, reflecting God’s just punishment of wrongdoers and reward of the righteous.
rows.anchor: وخزيه : ما أصابه يوم بدر من الصغار والقتل ، والسبب فيما مني به من خزي الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz means a jab; devils goad people toward sins as riders jab animals to make them move, like the “urging” in 19:83.
rows.anchor: الهمز : النخس . والهمزات : جمع المرة منه . ومنه : مهماز الرائض . والمعنى : أن الشياطين يحثون الناس على المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek refuge voices earnest, repeated supplication and asks God to keep devils from approaching at all.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتعوذ من نخساتهم بلفظ المبتهل إلى ربه ، المكرر لندائه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the refuge is sought during Qur’an recitation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : عند تلاوة القرآن .

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the refuge is sought at death.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : عند النزع .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Until” may attach to “they describe,” making their false descriptions last until this pause; the verse interrupts to reinforce ignoring them and seeking God’s help against Satan’s incitement to retaliate. Alternatively it attaches to “they are liars.”
rows.anchor: حتى } يتعلق بيصفون ، أي : لا يزالون على سوء الذكر إلى هذا الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural address to God is for exaltation, as in the cited poetic forms of address.
rows.anchor: خطاب الله بلفظ الجمع للتعظيم ، كقوله : فإن شئت حرمت النساء سواكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, seeing the truth brings remorse for neglected faith and good works, so the dying person asks to return and do what was left of faith.
rows.anchor: إذا أيقن بالموت واطلع على حقيقة الأمر ، أدركته الحسرة على ما فرط فيه من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that I may do good in what I left” means hoping to perform the faith omitted earlier, like building on a foundation means first laying that foundation.
rows.anchor: لعلي آتي بما تركته من الإيمان ، وأعمل فيه صالحا ، كما تقول : لعلي أبني على أس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the dying person asks to return to use the wealth he left behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فيما تركت من المال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that a believer offered return by the angels refuses the world of troubles and asks to proceed to God, while the unbeliever says, “Lord, return me.”
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إذا عاين المؤمن الملائكة قالوا : نرجعك إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes and rejects the request to return.
rows.anchor: كلا } ردع عن طلب الرجعة ، وإنكار واستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The word” means this connected portion of speech, the request to do good in what was left.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكلمة : الطائفة من الكلام المنتظم بعضها مع بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He will say it” means he cannot stop repeating it under grief and regret, or that only he says it and no answer is granted.
rows.anchor: هو قائلها } لا محالة ، لا يخليها ولا يسكت عنها لاستيلاء الحسرة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh is the barrier ahead of the dead until resurrection; it does not mean they return at resurrection, which is only a return to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أمامهم حائل بينهم وبين الرجعة إلى يوم البعث ، وليس المعنى : أنهم يرجعون يوم البعث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ṣūr with fatḥa on the waw.
rows.anchor: الصور بفتح الواو عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin is reported to read ṣūr with either kasra or fatḥa, supporting the interpretation that it means a collection of forms.
rows.anchor: والصور بالكسر والفتح عن أبي رزين . وهذا دليل لمن فسر الصور بجمع الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of kinship may mean people are separated into punishment and reward, with deeds replacing family ties; kinship also fails to prompt compassion as each flees relatives.
rows.anchor: ونفي الأنساب : يحتمل أن التقاطع يقع بينهم حيث يتفرقون معاقبين ومثابين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “they will not ask one another,” assimilating ta into sin.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : ( لا يساءلون ) بإدغام التاء في السين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent contradictions with 70:10, 37:27, 52:25 and 10:45 have two solutions: different periods and states during the fifty-thousand-year Day, or nonrecognition at the first blast followed by recognition and questions after the second.
rows.anchor: فيه جوابان ، أحدهما : أن يوم القيامة مقداره خمسون ألف سنة ، ففيه أزمنة وأحوال مختلفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the scales as weights of deeds, especially good deeds valued by God, citing 18:105.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الموازين : جمع موزون ؟ وهي الموزونات من الأعمال : أي الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Abiding in Hell” may be an apposition to “they lost themselves,” a predicate after “those,” or a predicate with an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: في جهنم خالدون } بدل من خسروا أنفسهم ، ولا محل للبدل والمبدل منه ؛ لأن الصلة لا محل لها . أو خبر بعد خبر لأولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talfaḥ means to scorch or sear.
rows.anchor: تلفح } تسفع . وقال الزجاج :

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says lafḥ and nafḥ are alike, except lafḥ has a stronger effect.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : اللفح والنفح واحد ، إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips retracting from the teeth, like the heads of roasted animals.
rows.anchor: والكلوح : أن تتقلص الشفتان وتتشمرا عن الأسنان ، كما ترى الرؤوس المشوية

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says seeing a head taken from an oven in the market caused ʿUtba al-Ghulam’s repentance and left him unconscious for three days.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار : كان سبب توبة عتبة الغلام أنه مر في السوق برأس أخرج من التنور

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report describes Hell retracting the upper lip to the middle of the head and dropping the lower lip to the navel.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “they are scorched,” with the alternative form kulihun.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( كلحون ) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads “because there was a group,” with fatḥa on anna to express causation.
rows.anchor: في حرف أبي : ( أنه كان فريق ) بالفتح ، بمعنى : لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukhriyy with kasra means mockery; with ḍamma it means subjection or enslavement. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh prefer the first account, while al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’ distinguish them by vowel.
rows.anchor: وعن الكسائي والفراء : أن المكسور من الهزء ، والمضموم من السخرة والعبودية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The believers mocked by the unbelievers may be the Companions generally or specifically the People of the Bench.
rows.anchor: قيل : هم الصحابة وقيل : أهل الصفة خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You took them for ridicule” means mockingly occupying yourselves with them; this behavior made you forget remembrance of God and fear for His friends.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : اتخذتموهم هزؤا وتشاغلتم بهم ساخرين { حتى أنسوكم } بتشاغلكم بهم على تلك الصفة { ذكرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, anna begins a new clause: they succeeded because they endured; with fatḥa, it is the object of “I rewarded them,” as in rewarding someone their success.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { أنهم } بالفتح ، فالكسر استئناف ، أي : قد فازوا حيث صبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan codices have “He said,” while the codices of the two sanctuaries, Basra and Syria have “Say.”
rows.anchor: قال } في مصاحف أهل الكوفة . وقل : في مصاحف أهل الحرمين والبصرة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With “He said,” the speaker may be God or an angel commanded to question them; in “He said, how long…,” the speaker may be the angel or a chief of Hell’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ففي { قال } ضمير الله أو المأمور بسؤالهم من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds are “ranged” by extending their wings in the air; the pronoun in “He knows” may refer to each creature or to God, as may the pronouns in prayer and praise.
rows.anchor: صافات } يصففن أجنحتهن في الهواء . والضمير في { علم } لكل أو لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer means supplication; God may inspire birds to pray and praise Him as He inspires subtle forms of knowledge beyond ordinary human understanding.
rows.anchor: والصلاة : الدعاء . ولا يبعد أن يلهم الله الطير دعاءه وتسبيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzji means to drive gently, as in an unwanted, low-grade commodity that everyone passes along.
rows.anchor: يزجي } يسوق . ومنه : البضاعة المزجاة : التي يزجيها كل أحد لا يرضاها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cloud may be singular or collective; composing one cloud means gathering scattered pieces, so “between it” refers to its parts, as in the poetic place names Dukhul and Hawmal.
rows.anchor: ومعنى تأليف الواحد : أنه يكون قزعا فيضم بعضه إلى بعض . وجاز بينه وهو واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukam is piled cloud, wadq is rain, and khilal are openings; a reading has the singular collective khalal.
rows.anchor: والركام : المتراكم بعضه فوق بعض . والودق : المطر { من خلاله } من فتوقه ومخارجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include intensified yunzilu, assimilated yakadu sana, different forms for lightning flashes and their quantity, and sanaa with short vowel meaning light or long vowel meaning height.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( من خلله ) { وينزل } بالتشديد ، ويكاد سنا : على الإدغام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المدني
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani reads “takes away sight” with an extra bā’, as in 2:195.
rows.anchor: و { يذهب بالأبصار } على زيادة الباء ، كقوله : { ولا تلقوا بأيديكم } ( البقرة : 195 ) عن أبي جعفر المدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain, lightning, and alternation of night and day are clear proofs of God’s lordship and attributes, showing His control of mercy, warning observers to reflect.
rows.anchor: وهذا من تعديد الدلائل على ربوبيته وظهور أمره ، حيث ذكر تسبيح من في السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet knew the unseen acts described here through God’s revelation, which explains “Have you not seen?”
rows.anchor: علمه من جهة إخبار الله إياه بذلك على طريق الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three min phrases may respectively mark origin, partitive division and explanation; alternatively, the first two mark origin and the last is partitive.
rows.anchor: قلت : الأولى لابتداء الغاية ، والثانية للتبعيض . والثالثة للبيان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mountains of hail” may mean God creates literal mountains of hail in heaven, or it may express great abundance, as in mountains of gold.
rows.anchor: قلت : فيه معنيان . أحدهما : أن يخلق الله في السماء جبال برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zodiac signs are stations for the seven planets, named after lofty towers because they house those planets; burj derives from conspicuous display.
rows.anchor: البروج : منازل الكواكب السبعة السيارة : الحمل ، والثور ، والجوزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siraj means the sun, as in 71:16; a reading in the plural includes the sun and the larger nearby planets.
rows.anchor: والسراج : الشمس كقوله تعالى : { وجعل الشمس سراجا } ( نوح : 16 ) وقرىء : ( سرجا )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Aʿmash read “and a moonlit night,” using qamrāʾ as a collective for moonlit nights with an omitted “possessing.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش : ( وقمرا منيرا ) وهي جمع ليلة قمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, qamar may be a dialectal form, like rushd/rushud or ʿarab/ʿarab.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون القمر بمعنى القمر ؛ كالرشد والرشد ، والعرب والعرب

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan’s line about Barada flowing with wine exemplifies retaining the force of an omitted possessive noun: the water of Barada.
rows.anchor: ونظيره في بقاء حكم المضاف بعد سقوطه وقيام المضاف إليه مقامه قول حسان :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse reaches its point concisely by mentioning the two sides under the theme of divine victory after initially omitting them.
rows.anchor: اختصر الطريق إلى الغرض بأن أدرج تحت ذكر الانتصار والنصر ذكر الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling believers’ victory “a duty upon Us” honors them as deserving divine aid and victorious success.
rows.anchor: تعظيم للمؤمنين ، ورفع من شأنهم ، وتأهيل لكرامة سنية ، وإظهار لفضل سابقة ومزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may pause after “truly,” making the phrase mean that vengeance was truly due, then begin “upon Us is aid of believers.”
rows.anchor: وقد يوقف على { حقا } . ومعناه : وكان الانتقام منهم حقا ، ثم يبتدأ : { علينا نصر المؤمنين }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says whoever protects a Muslim brother from harm has a duty from God that He protect him from Hell on Resurrection Day; the Prophet then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 847 ) ( ما من امرىء مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sometimes spreads the cloud continuously and sometimes makes it into fragments; rain emerges from it in either arrangement.
rows.anchor: فيبسطه } متصلا تارة { ويجعله كسفا } أي قطعا تارة { فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The sky” means the direction or expanse above, as in 14:24.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسماء . سمت السماء وشقها ، كقوله تعالى : { وفرعها في السماء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain reaching the servants means reaching their lands and territories.
rows.anchor: وبإصابة العباد : إصابة بلادهم وأراضيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before it” repeats for emphasis, as in 59:17, stressing how long they had been without rain, so their despair deepened and their joy matched it.
rows.anchor: من قبلهم } من باب التكرير والتوكيد ، كقوله تعالى : { فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They saw it” refers to the effect of God’s mercy, namely vegetation; a plural reading refers to the meaning because nabat is a verbal noun used for little or much growth.
rows.anchor: فرأوا أثر رحمة الله . لأن رحمة الله هي الغيث ، وأثرها : النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-in introduces an oath with a conditional clause; la-ẓallū answers both the oath and condition.
rows.anchor: ولئن : هي اللام الموطئة للقسم ، دخلت على حرف الشرط ، و { لظلوا } جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God condemns people who despair when rain is withheld, rejoice when it comes, then complain and disbelieve when a wind yellows crops; they should trust, give thanks and endure.
rows.anchor: ذمهم الله تعالى بأنه إذا حبس عنهم القطر قنطوا من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind may be a hot or northern dry wind, either of which withers vegetation; “yellow” describes a new discoloration, or refers to clouds turning yellow and not raining.
rows.anchor: والريح التي اصفر لها النبات : يجوز أن تكون حرورا وحرجفا ، فكلتاهما مما يصوح له النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿf is read with either fatḥa or ḍamma, both dialects; ḍamma is stronger because Ibn ʿUmar recited fatḥa to the Prophet and was corrected to ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بفتح الضاد وضمها ، وهما لغتان . والضم أقوى في القراءة ، لما روى ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : قال :

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reported that when he recited “min ḍaʿf” with fatḥa, the Prophet taught him the ḍamma reading.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : قال : ( 848 ) قرأتها على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من ضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being created “from weakness” describes the human constitution: weakness in infancy, strength from maturity to adulthood, and a return to weakness in old age.
rows.anchor: يعني أن أساس أمركم وما عليه جبلتكم وبنيتكم الضعف { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the initial weakness is the drop, as in 32:8 and 77:20.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من ضعف من النطف ، كقوله تعالى : { من ماء مهين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing people through these successive conditions is a clear proof of the Creator’s knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترديد في الأحوال المختلفة ، والتغيير من هيئة إلى هيئة وصفة إلى صفة : أظهر دليل وأعدل شاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of what lies in hearts explains His knowledge of the unseen, since the hidden contents of hearts are the most concealed things.
rows.anchor: كالتعليل ، لأنه إذا علم ما في الصدور وهو أخفى ما يكون فقد علم غيب في العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhat al-sudur means the hidden contents of hearts; dhat is the feminine of dhu, denoting something accompanying another, as pregnancy accompanies a belly and drink a vessel.
rows.anchor: وذات الصدور : مضمراتها ، وهي تأنيث ذو في نحو قول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه : ذو بطن خارجة جارية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abu Bakr’s expression “the one with the belly of Kharija is pregnant” illustrates dhu meaning accompaniment.
rows.anchor: قول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه : ذو بطن خارجة جارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line about the contents of a vessel likewise illustrates an accompanying thing; the wording “with it is a rope” confirms the usage.
rows.anchor: المعنى ما في بطنها من الحبل ، وما في إنائك من الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalifa has plural khalāʾif and khalif has plural khulafāʾ; people are God’s successors, entrusted with earthly control and its benefits so they may thank Him through unity and obedience.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه جعلكم خلفاءه في أرضه قد ملككم مقاليد التصرف فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief denies this great gift and brings its consequence back on the disbeliever: God’s loathing and ultimate loss; maqt is the strongest hatred, hence the term for one marrying his father’s wife.
rows.anchor: فوبال كفره راجع عليه ، وهو مقت الله الذي ليس وراءه خزي وصغار وخسار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to all people; alternatively, it addresses the Prophet’s audience as a nation succeeding earlier peoples and able to learn from their observed fate.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب للناس . وقيل : خطاب لمن بعث إليهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭams is erasing the eye’s slit until it is wiped away.
rows.anchor: الطمس : تعفية شق العين حتى تعود ممسوحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Race to the path” may elide the preposition, incorporate the sense of hastening, make the path a goal, or use it adverbially.
rows.anchor: فاستبقوا الصراط } لا يخلو من أن يكون على حذف الجار وإيصال الفعل . والأصل : فاستبقوا إلى الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God blinded them, they could not race along their familiar road to homes and familiar destinations; habitual routes would defeat them, like blind people who know only well-practiced places.
rows.anchor: لو شاء لمسح أعينهم ، فلو راموا أن يستبقوا إلى الطريق المهيع الذي اعتادوا سلوكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say they could neither run the familiar way when blinded nor leave it for unfamiliar roads.
rows.anchor: أو لو شاء لأعماهم ، فلو طلبوا أن يخلفوا الصراط الذي اعتادوا المشي فيه لعجزوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading “in their places” has a plural variant; makanah and makan mean the same, like maqamah and maqam.
rows.anchor: على مكانتهم ) وقرىء : ( على مكاناتهم ) والمكانة والمكان واحد ، كالمقامة والمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could transform them so they were fixed in place, unable to go forward or backward.
rows.anchor: لمسخناهم مسخا يجمدهم مكانهم لا يقدرون أن يبرحوه بإقبال ولا إدبار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the transformation would make them apes and pigs.
rows.anchor: واختلف في المسخ ، فعن ابن عباس : لمسخناهم قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they would become stones.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حجارة .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they would be made to sit on their feet and immobilized.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة : لأقعدناهم على أرجلهم وأزمناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for going forward has three vocalized readings, compared with the different forms of ʿata and ṣabi.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( مضيا ) بالحركات الثلاث ، فالمضي والمضي كالعتي والعتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ guidance comprises all religious gifts, including signs, the Torah and religious laws; God left the Torah to the Children of Israel as guidance and reminder.
rows.anchor: يريد بالهدى : جميع ما آتاه في باب الدين من المعجزات والتوراة والشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guidance and reminder” may be accusative as purpose or nominative-like circumstantial descriptions.
rows.anchor: هدى وذكرى } إرشادا وتذكرة ، وانتصابهما على المفعول له أو على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of understanding are believers in the Torah who act according to it.
rows.anchor: وأولوا الألباب : المؤمنون به العاملون بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashiʿin means diminished and humbled by disgrace; “from humiliation” may attach to “looking,” and a pause may follow khashiʿin.
rows.anchor: خاشعين } متضائلين متقاصرين مما يلحقهم { من الذل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking from a furtive glance means beginning with faint eyelid movement, like a condemned person glancing at a sword; fear prevents opening the eyes fully as one does toward what one loves.
rows.anchor: ينظرون من طرف خفى } أي يبتدىء نظرهم من تحريك لأجفانهم ضعيف خفي بمسارقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they are gathered blind and look only with their hearts; al-Zamakhshari calls this strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يحشرون عميا فلا ينظرون إلا بقلوبهم . وذلك نظر من طرف خفي . وفيه تعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “On the Day of Resurrection” may modify “they lost,” making the believers’ words worldly, or modify “he said,” making them speak after seeing the unbelievers’ state.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة } إما أن يتعلق بخسروا ، ويكون قول المؤمنين واقعا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person obeys and follows the soul’s desire as though worshipping it like a deity.
rows.anchor: أي : هو مطواع لهوى النفس يتبع ما تدعوه إليه ، فكأنه يعبده كما يعبد الرجل إلاهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “gods of his desire”: he might worship one stone, then replace it with a more appealing one, effectively serving many gods.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( آلهة هواه ) ، لأنه كان يستحسن الحجر فيعبده ، فإذا رأى ما هو أحسن رفضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s misguidance may mean abandoning and withholding guidance and grace, knowing it would not benefit him; alternatively it is with knowledge of the routes of guidance and all beneficial favors.
rows.anchor: وأضله الله على علم } وتركه عن الهداية واللطف وخذله على علم ، عالما بأن ذلك لا يجدى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings vary the vowels of gishawah and include the forms ghashwah and tadhakkarun.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( غشاوة ) بالحركات الثلاث . وغشوة ، بالكسر والفتح . وقرىء ( تتذكرون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Is this not true?” is quoted after an omitted “it is said”; “this” means the punishment, as confirmed by “taste the punishment,” and sarcastically rebukes those who mocked God’s promise and threat.
rows.anchor: أليس هاذا بالحق } محكى بعد قول مضمر ، وهذا المضمر هو ناصب الظرف . وهذا إشارة إلى العذاب ، بدليل قوله تعالى : { فذوقوا العذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulu al-ʿazm means messengers of resolve, steadfastness and patience.
rows.anchor: العزم } أولوا الجد والثبات والصبر . و { من } يجوز أن تكون للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If min is partitive, the resolute messengers include Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David and Jesus, each enduring the trials listed.
rows.anchor: قيل : هم نوح ، صبر على أذى قومه : كانوا يضربونه حتى يغشى عليه ، وإبراهيم على النار وذبح ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min explains the phrase, so all messengers are resolute; 20:115 says Adam lacked resolve and 68:48 warns against the Companion of the Fish.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون للبيان ، فيكون أولو العز صفة الرسل كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not ask that Quraysh’s punishment be hastened: it will surely come, and then they will deem their worldly stay no more than an hour.
rows.anchor: ولا تستعجل } لكفار قريش بالعذاب ، أي : لا تدع لهم بتعجيله ؛ فإنه نازل بهم لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A conveyance” may mean that the warning is sufficient admonition, or that it is the Messenger’s delivery.
rows.anchor: بلاغ } أي هذا الذي وعظتم به كفاية في الموعظة . أو هذا تبليغ من الرسول عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include balagha, balaghan, two forms of yahlak, and nahlik with first-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( يهلك ) بفتح الياء وكسر اللام وفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the immoral people are destroyed.
rows.anchor: إلا القوم الفاسقون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for every grain of sand in the world to whoever recites Surat al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1035 ) ( من قرأ سورة الأحقاف كتب له عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person “with a heart” has an attentive, receptive heart; one who does not understand is as if heartless.
rows.anchor: لمن كان له قلب } أي قلب واع ؛ لأن من لا يعي قلبه فكأنه لا قلب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening means attending; “while he is a witness” may mean mentally present, a believer witnessing revelation, or one of the witnesses mentioned in 2:143.
rows.anchor: وإلقاء السمع : الإصغاء { وهو شهيد } أي حاضر بفطنته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the witness is a member of the People of the Book who recognizes the Qur’an’s truth from its description in their scripture.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة وهو شاهد على صدقه من أهل الكتاب لوجود نعته عنده

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others read the phrase passively: someone else opens the listener’s ear, but the person remains present-minded and attentive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السدي وجماعة ( ألقى السمع ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation supplies “his”: he gives his own hearing to the message.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ألقى سمعه أو السمع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lughub means fatigue; a reading puts fatḥa on ghayn, like the forms qabul and wuluʿ.
rows.anchor: اللغوب الإعياء . وقرىء بالفتح بزنة القبول والولوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is said to answer Jews who claimed God created the heavens and earth in six days, rested on Saturday and reclined on the Throne; the anthropomorphism in the Muslim community was said to come from them.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت في اليهود لعنت تكذيبا لقولهم خلق الله السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be patient with what they say” may concern Jewish unbelief and anthropomorphism, or polytheists’ denial of resurrection, since the Creator of the world can resurrect and punish.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فاصبر على ما يقول المشركون من إنكارهم البعث ؛ فإن من قدر على خلق العالم قدر على بعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the patience command was abrogated by the sword verse; another view says patience is commanded in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي منسوخة بآية السيف . وقيل : الصبر مأمور به في كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise accompanies glorification; tasbih may be literal or prayer. The times correspond to Fajr before sunrise, Dhuhr and ʿAsr before sunset, and the two evening prayers or night vigil.
rows.anchor: والتسبيح محمول على ظاهره أو على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After prostration” may mean glorification after prayers, since prostration and bowing can denote prayer, or voluntary prayers after the obligatory ones.
rows.anchor: وأدبار السجود } التسبيح في آثار الصلوات ، والسجود والركوع يعبر بهما عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali says “after prostration” means the two rakʿas after Maghrib.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : الركعتان بعد المغرب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says prayer after Maghrib before speaking is recorded in the highest heaven.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1086 )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as the witr prayer after ʿIsha.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الوتر بعد العشاء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adbar is plural of dubur; a reading adbara means the time when prayer has ended, like coming when a star sets.
rows.anchor: والأدبار : جمع دبر . وقرىء : ( وأدبار ) من أدبرت الصلاة إذا انقضت وتمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Listen” directs attention to the report of Resurrection, magnifying the event and its announcement.
rows.anchor: استمع } يعني واستمع لما أخبرك به من حال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet told Muadh for seven days, “Listen, Muadh, to what I say,” before telling him.
rows.anchor: كما يروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( 1087 ) أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day the caller calls” governs the implied “they emerge”; “the day they hear the shout” apposes to it. Israfil calls as he blows the Trumpet, though another view assigns the call to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: المناد } إسرافيل ينفخ في الصور وينادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller’s nearby location may be the Jerusalem rock, twelve miles from heaven and at earth’s center; another view places it beneath their feet.
rows.anchor: من مكان قريب } من صخرة بيت المقدس ، وهي أقرب الأرض من السماء باثني عشر ميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the call comes from the roots of their hair, so every hair hears the summons.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من منابت شعورهم يسمع من كل شعرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shout is the second blast; “in truth” qualifies the blast, meaning resurrection and gathering for judgment.
rows.anchor: { الصيحة } النفخة الثانية { بالحق } متعلق بالصيحة
